A new mentoring program connects early-career engineers at the center with graduate students from regional universities, giving both groups a structured way to learn from one another. Participants meet monthly to discuss technical challenges, career decisions, and the practical realities of working on large teams. Program organizers say the goal is to strengthen the pipeline of talent into the aerospace workforce while giving experienced staff a chance to reflect on their own practices. "Mentoring is not a one-way street," said one program lead. "The students ask questions we have stopped asking ourselves, and that keeps all of us sharp." Over its first year, the program matched forty-two pairs, and surveys of participants showed that a large majority would recommend it to colleagues. Applications for the next cohort open in January and are available to students in any engineering or science discipline.
